origine.title: Christmas 1972
origine.subtitle: A pot of red paint, a pedal car, and a whole house to cross.
origine.description: I was seven. I drove too fast, knocked over the pot, and kept going. On the floorboards, the tyres left their marks, tracing the lines. My mother told me off. I thought it was beautiful. Fifty years on, I have simply found better wheels.

atelier.title: The studio
atelier.subtitle: A garage, a Dino, and twenty years of sleepless nights.
atelier.description: For twenty years, I got up in the middle of the night to go and paint, alone with my cars and a question that never left me: how do you represent movement through imprints on a canvas? The technique refined itself gradually — wheel speed, forward or reverse, density of the products, freshly primed canvases, rain sometimes. It is no longer a happy accident.

creations.title: Canvases & Photographs
creations.subtitle: The work of art that produces a work
creations.description: My canvases accumulate layers of paint like a road coating itself in grease, or the floor of a workshop after decades of oil changes. I can paint according to the speed of the wheel rotation — I roughly know what will happen. My photographs capture the instant when the Dino works on the canvas.

photographies.title: Three photographic series
photographies.subtitle: Imprints • Studio • Projections
photographies.description: The imprints show what the wheels and bodywork deposited on the canvas. The studio is the other side — the cars smeared in paint, the canvases stacked up, the floor covered. The projections capture the movement the instant it happens.

acquerir.subtitle: Numbered and signed prints
acquerir.description: Each photograph documents a moment of creation that will never recur. Numbered and signed prints, from A4 up to large format 2A0. Certificate of authenticity included.

histoire.title: On the trail of the Dino
histoire.subtitle: From the pedal car to the Meyerbeer garage
histoire.description: At eight, watching The Persuaders!, I already knew what I wanted: to be Danny Wilde. The Dino's aesthetic entered my child's heart, and it never left. I haunted the Toulouse dealership, collected the catalogues, tracked down a 250 GTO made of Chapy. The passion never let go.

artist.label: The Artist
artist.name: Guillaume Farré
artist.bio: At Christmas 1972, I knocked over a pot of red paint with my pedal car. The marks on the floorboards — I thought they were beautiful. Fifty years later, it is a Dino 246 GT that leaves its imprints — on canvases.

dino.title: The Dino
dino.subtitle: Chassis #04844, fresh from the 1972 Paris Motor Show on the Pozzi stand. She is as beautiful as Sophia Loren.

origin.label: The Origin
origin.title: From Danny Wilde to the Meyerbeer garage
origin.text1: At eight, watching The Persuaders!, I knew I wanted to be Danny Wilde. The Dino 246 GT entered my child's imagination that evening, and it never left. I haunted the Ferrari dealership in Toulouse, collected the catalogues, tracked down a 250 GTO made of Chapy, then one day, at thirty-three, I found her at the Meyerbeer garage in Nice.
origin.text2: When I was little, I wanted to be a racing driver or a thief. I became neither — but the Dino became my instrument, and the studio my circuit.

creative.label: Its Role
creative.title: My instrument of creation
creative.text1: The Dino is not kept under a cover. She works. The tyres print the canvas, the weight crushes the pigments, the wheel speed determines the pattern. I control forward, reverse, the density of the products. Sometimes I wait for the rain. It is no longer the happy accident of the pedal car — it is a technique I spent twenty years building.
creative.text2: As Guy Depré said: 'It is the work of art that produces a work.' The Dino does not decorate the studio. She transforms it.
